summary: Colbert County, AL lookout on private land inside Thomas WMA: a 100-foot wooden tower, replaced by steel after a 1950s lightning fire, removed around 2000.

facts.design: First a 100' wooden tower with exterior stairs; after a 1950s lightning fire, a standard 100' steel tower

access.note: Register lists the site as private property inside Thomas Wildlife Management Area

facts.status_note: Tower removed around 2000; only foundations remain, hard to find in thick brush.

events.note: Register says removed 'circa 2000'; land sold back to its original owner

evidence.supports: site is in Colbert County, Alabama
private property inside Thomas Wildlife Management Area
evidence.quote: This tower was located on private property inside Thomas Wildlife Management Area.

evidence.supports: Colbert County Forestry Office pictures indicate a 100-foot wooden tower with exterior stairs
evidence.quote: The Colbert County Forestry Office has pictures indicating Pope Lookout was originally built as a 100' wooden tower with exterior stairs.
This was later modified to have interior stairs.

evidence.supports: burned in the 1950s after a lightning strike; replaced with a standard 100-foot steel tower
evidence.quote: This tower burned in the 1950s after a lightning strike and was replaced with a standard 100' steel tower.

evidence.supports: administered by the Alabama Forestry Commission
removed around 2000; land sold back to its original owner
evidence.quote: The tower was removed around 2000 and the land sold back to its original owner.

evidence.supports: only foundations remain; hard to locate in thick brush
evidence.quote: Foundations are all that remain and are difficult to locate due to thick brush.

notes_for_editor: Single source (FFLOS detail page, which relays pictures held by the Colbert County Forestry Office; those pictures were not seen). The 1950s burn and replacement have no exact year, so no events were written for them; a decade-level event could be added if the timeline allows. No built year is given, so there is no built event. Record material 'steel' describes the structure at removal; the first tower was wooden per the register, so the material field may need 'wood, then steel'. Access rests only on the register's 'private property' wording; whether the surrounding WMA is open to the public was not checked.
